concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the opening stanza contrasts a crowded city with the refugees' lack of any place.
Interpret the images of the atlas and the yew tree that renews itself while old passports cannot.
Analyse how the consul and the committee show the cold indifference of official systems.
Interpret the speaker's claim that refugees 'will steal our daily bread' as prejudice against outsiders.

topics.title: Persecution and the contrast with animals and nature

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the historical context of Nazi persecution of German Jews in the poem.
Evaluate how the poodle, cat, fish and birds highlight the refugees' loss of freedom and dignity.

topics.title: Dreams denied and the final threat

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the dream of a building with a thousand doors, none of them the refugees'.
Explain how 'two tickets to Happiness' and the full coaches capture the essence of the poem.
Analyse the menace of the final stanza with ten thousand soldiers searching for the couple.

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ballad and blues form and the role of the refrain in the poem.
Distinguish irony, pathos and sarcasm as used in the poem.
